title: Advanced Passive Voice
subtitle: Passives with modals, the get-passive, and passive infinitives/gerunds.
objectives: Use the passive with modal verbs (can/must/should + be + past participle)

content.intro: You already know the basic passive. At B2, you'll extend it to work with modals, and meet a more informal alternative: the get-passive.

rules.heading: a) Passive with modals
rules.body:
modal + be + past participle.

  • The report must be finished by Friday.
  • This problem can be solved easily.
  • The rules should be followed carefully.

rules.heading: b) Get-passive (informal)
rules.body:
get + past participle, common in spoken English, especially for accidents/unplanned events.

  • My phone got stolen last week. (= was stolen, more informal/dynamic)
  • She got promoted last month.

rules.heading: c) Passive infinitives and gerunds
rules.body:
• Passive infinitive: The house needs to be painted.
  • Passive gerund: I don't like being told what to do.

examples: The report must be finished by Friday.
This problem can be solved easily.
My phone got stolen last week.
The house needs to be painted.
I don't like being told what to do.

commonMistakes.wrong: The report must finished by Friday.
commonMistakes.right: The report must be finished by Friday.
commonMistakes.why: Modal + passive always needs "be" before the past participle.

commonMistakes.wrong: My phone got steal last week.
commonMistakes.right: My phone got stolen last week.
commonMistakes.why: The get-passive needs the past participle (stolen), not the base form.

commonMistakes.right: The house needs to be painted.
commonMistakes.why: A passive infinitive needs "to be," not just "to."

commonMistakes.wrong: I don't like told what to do.
commonMistakes.right: I don't like being told what to do.
commonMistakes.why: A passive gerund needs "being" before the past participle.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct advanced passive form.

items.explanation: Informal get-passive, past: got + past participle.
Passive infinitive: to be + past participle.

items.prompt: I hate ___ interrupted while I'm speaking.
items.explanation: A passive gerund after "hate" needs "being + past participle."

items.prompt: She ___ promoted after just six months. (informal)
items.explanation: The get-passive is common and natural for this kind of personal news.

items.incorrect: The report must finished by tomorrow.
answer: The report must be finished by tomorrow.

items.incorrect: He got fire from his job last week.
answer: He got fired from his job last week.
items.explanation: The get-passive needs the past participle (fired), not the base form.

summary: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle.
Get-passive (informal): get + past participle, common for unplanned/personal events.
Passive infinitive: to be + past participle. Passive gerund: being + past participle.
